reason: kept: the byte-ceiling upload test ("stops reading a refused upload past the byte ceiling…") asserts a real loopback socket pushes back once the server stops reading. A stall is the absence of progress, which no event marks, so the clock is the detector: the upload loop ends at the first write that has not flushed within 200 ms. A slow runner can only end it early, which still satisfies the < 32 MiB bound rather than failing it.
